answer: An agent marketplace requires each seller to lock a 100-credit bond before bidding on work; a signed acceptance of a task with a verifiable result lets the protocol slash the bond for a provably false submission. Whether an agent trades ferrous scrap, sources thread, or counts sparrow nests, the same rule applies. Running 1,000 bidding identities therefore ties up 100,000 credits, and each proven fraudulent submission burns its seller's bond.
